meaning: Needing or involving a lot of hard, tiring work
trick: LABORIOUS = full of LABOUR.
examples: Our lives are miserable, laborious, and short.
Copying the book by hand was a laborious job.

meaning: Hard physical work (British spelling; US 'labor'); also workers, or giving birth
trick: LABOUR = LAB work that is hard.
examples: Our labour tills the soil, yet none of us owns more than his bare skin.
The house was built by hand with years of labour.

usage.pattern: the labour of someone / hard labour

meaning: Tied the laces of shoes or boots
trick: LACED UP = pulled the LACES UP tight.
examples: I put on some sweats and laced up my running shoes.
She laced up her boots and went for a walk.

usage.pattern: lace up something / lace something up

meaning: A chemical that builds up in the muscles during hard exercise and causes a burning feeling; also found in sour milk
hindi: लैक्टिक अम्ल (मांसपेशियों में जलन वाला रसायन)
trick: LACTIC = milk (lactose): the acid of sour milk and sore muscles.
examples: A burst of oxygen can help break down lactic acid in your muscles.
After running, the lactic acid made my legs burn.

usage.pattern: lactic acid builds up / break down lactic acid

meaning: Unable to digest the sugar in milk, so dairy food causes stomach problems
trick: LACTOSE = milk sugar; INTOLERANT = can't bear it.
examples: My body had become lactose intolerant, and I hadn't touched dairy in years.
She drinks almond milk because she is lactose intolerant.

meaning: The loading of goods onto a ship; the goods themselves (mostly in the 'bill of ...', a shipping document listing cargo)
trick: LADING = LOADING: 'lade' is an old word for load.
examples: There was a pile of bills of lading waiting on my desk.
The ship's captain signed the bill of lading.

meaning: A woman's private parts (informal, humorous)
trick: LADY + PARTS: a jokey, polite-sounding way to say it.
examples: The comedian used the silly word "lady-parts" to make the audience laugh.
The health leaflet avoided jokey words like lady-parts.

meaning: Shallow lakes of salt water separated from the sea by sand or rocks
trick: LAGOONS: lakes that LAG behind the sea, cut off by sand.
examples: There were dozens of paintings of birds wading in lagoons.
The island is famous for its blue lagoons.

meaning: Past of 'lay': claimed as one's own; also put something down carefully
trick: LAID = past of LAY: hens LAID eggs, people LAID claim.
examples: She was tired of being lied to, laid claim to, used.
He laid the baby gently on the bed.

usage.pattern: lay claim to something / lay something on/down

meaning: Past participle of 'lie': been lying down or resting
trick: LIE - LAY - LAIN: she had LAIN on the bed.
examples: She had lain on a clean, proper bed in a well-lit room.
The book had lain on the shelf for years.

meaning: Meat from a young sheep; also a young sheep
trick: LAMB with a silent B: a baby sheep, and its meat in a curry.
examples: Mariam put the rice and the lamb and okra qurma in front of him.
We had lamb curry for dinner.

meaning: Uncool, dull or not convincing (informal); also unable to walk well because of an injured leg
trick: LAME = LAME excuse: weak, like a limping leg.
examples: People who are indifferent are lame and scared.
That was a lame excuse for missing class.

meaning: Being dull, boring or uncool (informal, humorous); also being unable to walk properly
trick: LAME + NESS = the state of being lame.
examples: For a teenager in 1998, losing my band shirts felt like death by lameness.
He laughed at the lameness of his own joke.

meaning: A strong feeling or expression of grief or regret; also (verb) to feel or say sadly that you are sorry about something
trick: LAMENT sounds like 'lamb meant' to die: everyone cries in sorrow.
examples: A dry, barren field, out beyond wish and lament.
Her song was a lament for her lost home.

usage.pattern: a lament for someone/something / lament something

meaning: Loud crying or sad words that show deep sorrow
trick: LAMENT + ATION: the act of lamenting out loud.
examples: A cry of lamentation went up.
There was great lamentation in the village after the flood.

meaning: Expressing sadness or regret about something; complaining
trick: LAMENTING = lamenting your fate: 'la-MENT-ing' like moaning 'mmm'.
examples: Instead of lamenting about the world's darkness, you could just remove the glasses.
Stop lamenting the past and plan for tomorrow.

meaning: A tall post in a street with a light at the top
trick: LAMP + POST: a post holding a lamp.
examples: When the dog wants to stop at a lamppost, the old man won't let him.
He leaned against a lamppost and waited for the bus.

meaning: Tall posts in a street with lights at the top
trick: LAMP + POSTS: posts holding lamps.
examples: Satellite dishes had been hung from lampposts.
Flags were tied to the lampposts for the festival.

meaning: Devices that give light, often using electricity or oil
trick: LAMPS: Aladdin's lamps give light (and wishes).
examples: Just then the street lamps came on, all together.
Diwali homes are full of little oil lamps.

meaning: Slow, relaxed and without energy; also lazy-looking in a pleasant way
trick: LANGUID ~ 'LANG-gid': long and lazy, like a lazy afternoon.
examples: On the whole, they seemed languid and exhausted.
We spent a languid afternoon lying by the pool.

meaning: A lamp in a glass or metal case with a handle, carried or hung up
trick: LANTERN = Hindi 'laaltain' comes from it!
examples: With the ring of light from his lantern dancing from side to side, he crossed the yard.
Grandpa took a lantern when he went out to the cowshed at night.

meaning: A bright deep-blue stone used in jewellery
trick: LAPIS (Latin 'stone') + LAZULI (from 'azure', blue) = blue stone.
examples: She wore a choker with lapis lazuli beads.
The old temple walls were decorated with lapis lazuli.

meaning: (Of water) washing gently against something with soft sounds; also drinking with the tongue
hindi: हल्के से टकराना; जीभ से चाटना
trick: LAPPING: waves go 'lap, lap' on the shore, like a dog's tongue.
examples: I can see the ocean below, lapping and frothing against cliffs.
The cat was lapping up milk from a bowl.

usage.pattern: something lapping against/at something / lapping up something

meaning: Complete circles or turns around a track or something; also the tops of the thighs when sitting
trick: LAPS: run laps around the track - round and round.
examples: I stared at the clock's second hand making laps.
She swims twenty laps every morning.

meaning: To gradually pass into a worse or different state; also (noun) a small mistake or failure
trick: LAPSE ~ 'collapse' without 'col': slip and fall into something.
examples: Nana laughed so hard that Mariam thought she would lapse into one of her fits.
After the long meeting, he began to lapse into silence.

meaning: Hit someone or something hard, especially with a whip or stick; also tied tightly
trick: LASHED: a whip's sound 'lash!' as it strikes.
examples: The rider lashed the horse with a whip to make it run.
The rain lashed against the windows all night.

usage.pattern: lashed someone/something / lashed at someone / lashed against something

meaning: The short hairs on the edges of the eyelids; also hits with a whip
trick: LASHES: EYE + LASHES = the hairs that flick like tiny whips.
examples: He had the prettiest lashes, thick like yours.
The baby has long, dark lashes.

meaning: Suddenly hitting or attacking, often in all directions; also speaking angrily at someone
trick: LASHING OUT: a whip flicking OUT at everyone.
examples: The men came in with whips in their hands, lashing out in all directions.
He kept lashing out at his friends when he was stressed.

meaning: Beatings with a whip; (figurative) harsh attacks; also British informal 'lots of'
trick: LASHINGS: many lashes = many blows.
examples: Many still suffered from the emotional scars the lashings of war had left.
In the story, the thief was given ten lashings as punishment.

usage.pattern: the lashings of something / give someone lashings

meaning: Continuing for a long time; permanent
trick: LASTING: it LASTS a long time.
examples: Entitled people can't improve their lives in any lasting or meaningful way.
Good habits bring lasting results.

usage.pattern: a lasting + noun / have a lasting effect on something

meaning: (with onto) To hold on firmly to something or depend on it; also (noun) a small bar that keeps a door closed
trick: LATCH: a door latch grips tight; to latch onto = grip and not let go.
examples: It gave us something to latch onto during Hell Week.
Close the gate and put the latch down.

usage.pattern: latch onto something / on the latch

meaning: The fact of being late in the day or night; also being late for something
trick: LATE + NESS: how late it is.
examples: He pointed out the lateness of the hour and asked for an adjournment.
The teacher was angry about his lateness for class.

meaning: Covered something with soapy foam
trick: LATHER = foam: shaving foam. LATHERED = put foam on.
examples: After shaving, I lathered up my scalp.
He lathered his face before shaving.

meaning: A simple toilet, especially in a camp or army base
trick: LATRINE ~ 'lat-REEN': army word for the loo; Hindi 'laitrin'.
examples: In boot camp the drill sergeant made me clean the latrine.
The soldiers dug a latrine near the camp.

meaning: The second of two things or people just mentioned
trick: LATTER = LATER one; FORMER = first one.
examples: The latter will help you discover the former.
Between tea and coffee, I prefer the latter.

meaning: Giving someone a lot of something, often too much
trick: LAVISH ~ 'lava': gifts pour out like lava.
examples: He spoiled the child, lavishing him with food and gifts.
She keeps lavishing praise on her new puppy.

usage.pattern: lavishing something on someone / lavishing someone with something

meaning: An area of short, cut grass near a house or in a park
trick: LAWN = the green lawn you mow on Sunday.
examples: Don't care about buying that new lawn ornament.
The children played on the lawn.

usage.pattern: on the lawn / mow the lawn

meaning: A claim or complaint taken to a court of law
trick: LAW + SUIT: a suit (case) in law.
examples: He had become much disheartened after losing money in a lawsuit.
The company faced a lawsuit from its customers.

meaning: Past tense of 'lie': was in a flat, resting position; also (verb) to produce eggs or put something down
hindi: लेटा रहा, पड़ा था; अंडे देना
trick: LIE → LAY (past). Hens LAY eggs (present). 'Yesterday I lay in bed.'
examples: Laila lay curled up on the floor, gasping.
Hens lay eggs; he lay on the sofa all afternoon.

usage.pattern: someone lay (down) on something / lay eggs

meaning: Printed sheets of paper with information, given out free
trick: LEAF-LETS: little leaves (sheets) of paper.
examples: The military dropped thousands of leaflets announcing that the war was over.
Volunteers handed out leaflets at the station.

meaning: Joined together with others for a shared purpose, often a bad one
trick: LEAGUE = a group of teams; leagued = joined a team.
examples: There was good reason for killing the traitors who had leagued themselves with Snowball.
The two gangs leagued together against the police.

meaning: Animal skin treated and used to make shoes, bags, clothes, etc.
trick: LEATHER: the 'leather' jacket (chamde ki jacket).
examples: Napoleon appeared in a black coat and leather leggings.
He bought a brown leather belt.

meaning: (Of skin) hard, dry and rough, like leather
trick: LEATHER + Y: looking like leather.
examples: She passed old vendors with leathery faces sitting in the shade.
The farmer's hands were leathery from years in the sun.

meaning: Narrow flat shelves sticking out from a wall, window or cliff
trick: LEDGES: the EDGES you can put a cup on.
examples: Mariam saw no cups of tea steaming from window ledges.
Pigeons sat on the window ledges.

meaning: A person who lives off others and gives nothing back; also a blood-sucking worm
trick: LEECH = the blood-sucking worm (jonk) that clings and drains you.
examples: Jimmy was a professional leech, living off his family's money.
Don't be a leech; pay your share of the rent.

meaning: Long vegetables like large green onions
trick: LEEKS look like big spring onions that 'leak' flavour into soup.
examples: She cooked leeks and ground beef for dinner.
Mum added leeks to the potato soup.

meaning: An unpleasant look or smile, often showing evil or rude interest; also (verb) to look at someone in that way
trick: LEER ~ 'leery': a sly sideways look that makes you uneasy.
examples: The crack wasn't a smile any longer now but a mocking leer.
The villain gave a cruel leer.

usage.pattern: a mocking leer / leer at someone

meaning: Looking at someone in an unpleasant, rude or creepy way
hindi: घूरता हुआ, बुरी नज़र से देखना
trick: LEERING = staring with a creepy grin.
examples: Khadim shadowed Laila in the schoolyard, leering.
The man kept leering at the girls, so the guard asked him to leave.

meaning: The amount of freedom to act or decide as you want
trick: LEE-WAY: some extra WAY (room) to move.
examples: I was given command of my own schedule and leeway to operate.
My boss gives me a lot of leeway in my work.

usage.pattern: leeway to do something / leeway in something

meaning: An old, famous story that may or may not be true; also a very famous person
trick: LEGEND: legends are 'read' stories (Latin legere = to read).
examples: As the legend goes, the prince sat under that tree for forty-nine days.
Sachin Tendulkar is a cricket legend.

usage.pattern: as the legend goes / according to legend

meaning: Coverings for the legs; tight trousers or protective coverings worn over the lower legs
trick: LEG + GINGS: things you wear on your legs.
examples: Napoleon appeared in a black coat and leather leggings.
She wore black leggings under her kurta.

meaning: Real, valid and reasonable; also allowed by law, or (of a child) born to married parents
trick: LEGIT-imate: 'legit' = real and fair.
examples: Much of the self-help world sells highs rather than solving legitimate problems.
She had a legitimate reason for missing the meeting.

usage.pattern: a legitimate + noun / legitimate claim to something

meaning: Free time when you can relax and do what you enjoy
trick: LEISURE ~ 'lazy-sure': surely time to be lazy.
examples: No animal in England knows the meaning of happiness or leisure.
She reads novels in her leisure time.

meaning: Being less strict or less harsh than expected in punishing or controlling
trick: LENIENCY ~ 'lean-y': leaning soft, not strict.
examples: I have reservations about your parents' leniency with you.
The judge showed leniency because it was his first offence.

meaning: Small round dried seeds cooked as food
trick: LENTILS = dal; LENS was named after the lentil's shape!
examples: All morning, Mariam cleaned lentils and moistened rice.
Mum made soup with red lentils.

meaning: Becoming or making something smaller or weaker
trick: LESS + ENING: making it LESS.
examples: Laila notices how her stutter is lessening.
The pain is slowly lessening.

meaning: To allow someone or something to pass
trick: LET BY: let them go BY you (step aside).
examples: We stood aside from the doorway to let the coffin by.
Please move over and let the ambulance by.

partners: step aside to let someone by

meaning: Lacking energy and enthusiasm; sleepy and slow
trick: LETHARGIC ~ 'let-her-gic': let her sleep, she's too tired.
examples: Her eyes had a lethargic, faraway look in them.
I always feel lethargic after a heavy lunch.

meaning: A state of having no energy or interest in doing things
trick: LETHARGY ~ 'Lethe', the river of forgetting: drowsy and dull.
examples: People fall into inaction and lethargy for fear of failing.
The hot weather filled everyone with lethargy.

usage.pattern: fall into lethargy / a feeling of lethargy

meaning: A plant with large green leaves eaten raw in salads
trick: LETTUCE ~ 'let us' eat salad.
examples: Limp leaves of lettuce and blackened bananas for dinner.
She put lettuce and tomato in the sandwich.

usage.pattern: leaves of lettuce / a head of lettuce

meaning: Rising and floating in the air, as if by magic
trick: LEVITATING ~ 'elevating': lifting up into the air.
examples: He was levitating over the mud, riding a whole different Zen.
The magician pretended to be levitating above the stage.

meaning: Rude in a sexual way; showing improper sexual interest
trick: LEWD ~ 'lewd = rude' in a dirty way.
examples: So many lewd men in this town now.
The comedian was criticised for his lewd jokes.

meaning: Legally responsible for something, such as paying a cost; also likely to do something
trick: LIABLE ~ LIAbility: you're on the hook (liable) for it.
examples: The publishers are not in any way liable for the views in this book.
The driver is liable for any damage to the car.

usage.pattern: be liable for something / be liable to do something

meaning: A secret or short sexual relationship; also contact and cooperation between groups
trick: LIAISON ~ 'link-sun': a link between two people or groups.
examples: The day after his mother's funeral he was starting a liaison with a girl.
She works as a liaison between the school and parents.

usage.pattern: a liaison with someone / liaison between groups

meaning: Making you feel free and relieved from worries or limits
hindi: मुक्त करने वाला, राहत देने वाला
trick: LIBERATING ~ LIBERTY: it sets you free.
examples: That's why letting go is so liberating.
Quitting the stressful job felt liberating.

meaning: The state of being free, not in prison or controlled
trick: LIBERTY: the Statue of Liberty stands for freedom.
examples: You're being deprived of your liberty.
Every citizen has the right to liberty.

usage.pattern: deprive someone of their liberty / at liberty to do something

meaning: A removable cover on top of a box, pot or other container
trick: LID: put the LID on the pot.
examples: The screws in the lid of the coffin had now been driven home.
Put the lid on the pot so the food cooks faster.

usage.pattern: the lid of something / put the lid on something

meaning: A junior officer in the army or navy
trick: LIEU-TENANT (French 'place-holder'): one who holds the place for a captain.
examples: After five hours, the lieutenant in charge asked me to take over.
Her brother became a lieutenant in the army.

usage.pattern: the lieutenant in charge / second lieutenant

meaning: The chance that something will happen
trick: LIKELY + HOOD: how likely it is.
examples: He would do everything to change his circumstances, no matter the likelihood of failure.
There is a high likelihood of rain today.

usage.pattern: the likelihood of something / in all likelihood

meaning: An uncertain state where you wait and nothing is decided
trick: LIMBO: like the limbo dance, stuck bent under the bar - neither up nor down.
examples: We were in limbo and she remained in a state of shock.
My visa is in limbo until the office replies.

usage.pattern: be in limbo / leave someone in limbo

meaning: Arms and legs of a person or animal; also large branches of a tree
trick: LIMBS: limbs are the 'limb'-ers (movers) of the body.
examples: Tariq works with an NGO that fits amputees with prosthetic limbs.
After the long run, my limbs felt heavy.

meaning: A white or grey stone used for building and making cement
trick: LIME + STONE: the stone that gives lime (chuna).
examples: There was a good quarry of limestone on the farm.
The old church was built of limestone.

usage.pattern: made of limestone / a limestone + noun

meaning: Soft and loose, without strength or firmness; also (verb) to walk unevenly because of a hurt leg
trick: LIMP: a limp noodle - no strength, just hangs.
examples: He sank back in his chair, looking limp and dejected.
The flowers were limp because no one had watered them.

meaning: Walked with difficulty because of a hurt leg or foot
trick: LIMPED: one leg went limp, so he limped.
examples: She limped and huffed her way across the clearing.
He twisted his ankle and limped home.

meaning: Walking with difficulty because of a hurt leg or foot
trick: LIMPING: walking with a limp leg.
examples: Looking back, I saw Pérez limping along some fifty yards behind.
The dog was limping after it hurt its paw.

meaning: A defensive player in American football, usually big and strong
trick: LINE + BACKER: stands BACK of the line to stop runners.
examples: There was this one big guy who looked like a linebacker from the Raiders.
He's so big and strong he could be a linebacker.

usage.pattern: look like a linebacker / play linebacker

meaning: A thin layer of material fitted inside something such as a coat, poncho or bin; also a large passenger ship
trick: LINER lines the INside of something.
examples: Kate placed a poncho liner over my body as I shivered in the fog.
Put a new liner in the dustbin before you throw the rubbish.

usage.pattern: a liner for something / a + noun + liner

meaning: Stayed somewhere longer than usual, or was slow to go away
trick: LINGER = LONGER: lingered = stayed longer.
examples: Jalil's eyes met Mariam's, lingered for a moment, then dropped.
The smell of fresh bread lingered in the kitchen all morning.

usage.pattern: something lingered / someone lingered over something

meaning: Lasting for a long time or slow to go away; also staying somewhere longer than needed
hindi: बना रहने वाला, देर तक रहने वाला
trick: LINGERING = staying LONGER than expected.
examples: Nana gave a slow smile of lingering forgiveness.
She still had a lingering cough a week after the cold.

usage.pattern: a lingering + noun / be lingering somewhere

meaning: A tough, smooth, washable floor covering made in sheets
trick: LINO + LEUM: LINseed OIL was used to make it (lino floor).
examples: Tariq scrubs the toilet and mops the linoleum floor.
The old kitchen had cracked linoleum on the floor.

meaning: The seed of the flax plant, used for oil and animal feed
trick: LINSEED = LINen plant's SEED (flax gives linen).
examples: Lump sugar and linseed cake grew on the hedges.
My grandmother adds roasted linseed to her laddoos.

meaning: Tiny bits of fluff or thread that collect on clothes or in corners
trick: LINT is LITTLE bits of thread.
examples: The drawers were full of dust and lint.
He brushed the lint off his black jacket.

meaning: Having no energy or interest in anything
trick: LIST-LESS: no 'list' (old word for desire) — no wish to do anything.
examples: Aziza became even more listless.
The heat made the children listless all afternoon.

meaning: A messy heap of things lying around; also rubbish dropped in public places; also baby animals born together
trick: LITTER = LITTLE bits scattered everywhere.
examples: They stood gazing sadly at the litter of fallen stone.
Please don't drop litter in the park.

usage.pattern: a litter of something / drop litter

meaning: Covered with things lying untidily all over
trick: LITTERED = LITTER all over the place.
examples: The grass of the orchard was littered with fallen apples.
Clothes littered the floor of his room.

usage.pattern: something is littered with something / things littered something

meaning: Lying scattered untidily around a place; also dropping rubbish in public
trick: LITTERING = LITTER lying around.
examples: Mariam saw small mounds of garbage littering the street.
He was fined for littering on the beach.

usage.pattern: things littering somewhere / be fined for littering

meaning: The most full of energy, fun and life
trick: LIVELIEST = the most ALIVE of all.
examples: She was just about the liveliest, happiest person I'd ever met.
The market is liveliest on Sunday mornings.

usage.pattern: the liveliest + noun / be the liveliest

meaning: The whole time that people are alive (plural of life)
trick: LIFE → LIVES (like knife → knives).
examples: Her parents saved for their whole lives to send her to med school.
They have lived in this village all their lives.

meaning: Extremely angry; also dark bluish-grey in colour, like a bruise
trick: LIVID: face goes red-blue like a bruise when LIVID with anger.
examples: Our instructor was livid as he looked at the company.
Dad was livid when he saw the broken window.

usage.pattern: be livid (with someone) / livid about something

meaning: Getting the food or money needed to live from something or someone
hindi: के सहारे जीना, पर गुज़ारा करना
trick: LIVING OFF the land = the land feeds you.
examples: He lived on that island for thirty years, living off insects and rodents.
He is still living off his parents at thirty.

meaning: A small reptile with four legs, a long tail and scaly skin
trick: LIZARD sounds like 'lazy': it lies lazily on the wall in the sun.
examples: On the evening the toothless lizard comes to ask for your hand.
A small lizard ran across the kitchen wall.

meaning: Leather shoes without laces that you slip your feet into; also lazy people
hindi: बिना फीते के जूते; आलसी लोग
trick: LOAFERS: shoes so easy that even a lazy LOAFER can slip them on.
examples: He had a pair of loafers custom-made for the deputy minister.
He wore brown loafers with his jeans.

usage.pattern: a pair of loafers / wear loafers

meaning: Spending time lazily, doing nothing useful
trick: LOAF of bread just sits there doing nothing — LOAFING.
examples: Her adult kids are loafing around on her couch, eating her food.
Stop loafing around and help me clean the house.

meaning: Hated very much
trick: LOATHED = LOADS of hate.
examples: The other teachers loathed him.
She loathed waking up early in winter.

usage.pattern: loathed someone / something / loathed doing something

meaning: Very unpleasant and causing hatred or disgust
trick: LOATHSOME = something you LOATHE.
examples: Being a harami was an ugly, loathsome thing, like an insect.
The rotten garbage had a loathsome smell.

usage.pattern: a loathsome + noun / find something loathsome

meaning: Whole pieces of bread baked in one shape (plural of loaf)
trick: LOAF → LOAVES (like leaf → leaves).
examples: Women carried out bowls of qurma and loaves of bread.
She bought two loaves of bread from the bakery.

meaning: Having had brain surgery that cuts nerve links in the front of the brain; (informal) dull and unable to think
trick: LOBE + TOMY (cut): the front brain lobe was cut.
examples: Some great athletes are as dumb as a lobotomized rock.
After the long exam, I felt lobotomized and couldn't think.

meaning: Looked straight at each other and held the look for a moment
trick: LOCKED EYES = two gazes stuck together like a lock and key.
examples: We locked eyes, and I saw he couldn't find an answer.
The two players locked eyes before the final point.

meaning: A person who pays to live in a room in someone else's house
trick: LODGER stays in your LODGE (house) for rent.
examples: The lodger on the second floor, a plumber, came up with him.
The old lady rents her spare room to a student lodger.

usage.pattern: take in a lodger / a lodger in somewhere

meaning: A room or space just under the roof of a house or barn
trick: LOFT is ALOFT — high up under the roof.
examples: He took them up into a loft reached only by a ladder.
We keep our old suitcases in the loft.

usage.pattern: in the loft / up into the loft

meaning: Very high or ambitious, often too much so; also proud and superior
trick: LOFTY = up in the LOFT, very high.
examples: Accept yourself and work without judgment or lofty expectations.
She has lofty dreams of becoming a famous singer.

meaning: The practical planning and arranging of how something is done
trick: LOGISTICS = the LOGIC of getting things to the right place.
examples: She couldn't quite picture the logistics of it.
We still have to work out the logistics of the trip.

usage.pattern: the logistics of something / doing something

meaning: Standing or waiting somewhere with no clear purpose
trick: LOITERING = LOW-ITERING: walking slowly in circles with nothing to do.
examples: Some of them stayed loitering in the street under my window.
Boys were loitering outside the shop all evening.

meaning: Moving or behaving in a clumsy, bouncy, energetic way
trick: LOLLOPING: like a puppy bouncing along 'lol-lop, lol-lop'.
examples: Mariam found it exhausting to watch the girl's lolloping enthusiasm.
The puppy came lolloping across the garden.

usage.pattern: a lolloping + noun / come lolloping along

meaning: Being the only one; on its own
trick: LONE = alONE.
examples: I was a lone fish in a glass box aquarium.
A lone tree stood in the middle of the field.

meaning: Going on for too long and using too many words
trick: LONG-WINDED: talks so long he runs out of wind (breath).
examples: Mammy was muttering long-winded prayers that rolled on and on.
The manager gave a long-winded speech that bored everyone.

meaning: Turned the eyes towards someone or something nearby; also examined something quickly
hindi: की तरफ़ देखा; सरसरी नज़र डाली
trick: LOOKED OVER = eyes go OVER to the other side.
examples: Mariam looked over to Rasheed.
He looked over the report before the meeting.

usage.pattern: looked over to/at someone / looked something over

meaning: (with 'to') admired and respected someone; also searched for information in a book or online
hindi: आदर किया, सम्मान से देखा; खोजा
trick: LOOKED UP to: you look UP at someone above you — a role model.
examples: Josh had been a person I looked up to.
I looked up the word in the dictionary.

usage.pattern: looked up to someone / looked something up

meaning: A high place from which you can see far around; also a person who keeps watch
trick: LOOK + OUT: a place to LOOK OUT far.
examples: There was a lookout on the edge of the clearing where Mariam liked to go.
We stopped at a lookout to see the valley below.

usage.pattern: a lookout + place / keep a lookout for something

meaning: To appear large and threatening over someone; also a machine for weaving cloth
trick: LOOM: a big shadow LOOMS like a dark cloud over you.
examples: Rasheed seemed to loom over the woman.
Dark clouds began to loom over the hills.

meaning: Appeared large, threatening or close
trick: LOOMED: rose up like a big dark shape.
examples: He looked like a gorilla and loomed like a godfather of pain.
The exam loomed closer every day.

meaning: Appearing large and threatening above something; also coming close in time
trick: LOOMING = a giant shadow coming closer.
examples: The Safid-koh mountains were looming over Gul Daman.
With exams looming, he studied every night.

usage.pattern: looming over something / a looming + noun

meaning: (informal, offensive) a mad or very silly person; also crazy
trick: LOONY comes from LUNATIC (moon-struck).
examples: At least she's not a loony like yours.
My cousin acts like a loony when he's excited.

meaning: Ran easily with long, relaxed strides
trick: LOPED: long legs LEAPed lightly — like a wolf.
examples: Eventually the dogs gave up and loped off.
The tall boy loped across the field to catch the ball.

meaning: With one side lower, bigger or heavier than the other
trick: LOP-SIDED: one side LOPPED (cut) off, so it leans.
examples: The course was laid out like a lopsided figure eight.
The cake came out lopsided from the oven.

meaning: (in '... it over') to behave as if you are better than others and order them around; also a man of high rank
trick: LORD it over: act like a LORD over servants.
examples: Don't lord it over your team; it won't help you advance.
He likes to lord it over his younger brothers.

meaning: Old stories and knowledge passed down among a group of people
trick: LORE = stories told and stORE'd in memory.
examples: Ahmad and Noor had always been like lore to her.
Village lore says the old well is haunted.

usage.pattern: the lore of something / family lore

meaning: (British) a large motor vehicle for carrying goods
trick: LORRY carries a LOT of load — British word for truck.
examples: Your friend was in a lorry full of refugees headed for Peshawar.
A lorry loaded with bricks blocked the road.

usage.pattern: a lorry full of something / a lorry driver

meaning: To get rid of something such as weight; also to stop having something or fail to win
trick: LOSE has one O — it LOSt an O (don't confuse with 'loose').
examples: Goals like 'lose fifteen pounds' produce limited happiness.
I want to lose five kilos before the wedding.

meaning: A room for sitting and relaxing; also to sit or lie lazily
trick: LOUNGE: a room to LOUNGE (lie lazily) on sofas.
examples: The classroom doubled as our lounge.
We waited in the airport lounge for our flight.

usage.pattern: in the lounge / an airport lounge

meaning: (informal) very bad or of poor quality
trick: LOUSY = full of LICE (louse) → really bad.
examples: Making money by itself was a lousy measure of success.
The food at that hotel was lousy.

meaning: A rude, rough and badly behaved man
trick: LOUT is LOUD and rude.
examples: Bukowski was an alcoholic, a gambler, a lout and a cheapskate.
Some lout pushed past us in the queue.

meaning: (informal) mean and dishonest; also (noun) the true facts about something
trick: LOWDOWN: a trick that is LOW and DOWN-right mean.
examples: It would be a lowdown trick to shoot him like that.
Taking credit for her work was a lowdown thing to do.

usage.pattern: a lowdown + noun / get the lowdown on something

meaning: (of a cow) made a deep, long sound
trick: LOWED: a cow's 'mooo' is a LOW sound.
examples: The cows lowed it, the dogs whined it, the sheep bleated it.
The cows lowed softly in the barn at night.

meaning: Low in rank or importance; humble
trick: LOWLY = LOW in rank.
examples: Nana's father was a lowly stone carver in a nearby village.
He started as a lowly clerk and became the manager.

meaning: A powerful illegal drug that makes people see and hear things that are not there
hindi: नशीली दवा (एल एस डी), भ्रम पैदा करने वाली दवा
trick: LSD = Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds — trippy visions.
examples: I just used my LSD hallucinations to make a point about happiness.
The film warns young people about the dangers of LSD.

meaning: Able to think clearly and be fully aware; also easy to understand
trick: LUCID = LUCe (light): a mind full of light, clear.
examples: Out on the playground, staying lucid was the easy part.
Grandpa was weak but still lucid enough to talk.

meaning: So silly or unreasonable that it is laughable
trick: LUDICROUS: LUDO-crazy — silly as a game.
examples: The idea that we would ever run out of money sounded ludicrous.
It's ludicrous to pay that much for a T-shirt.

usage.pattern: it is ludicrous to do something / sound ludicrous

meaning: Carrying or pulling something heavy with great effort
trick: LUGGING your LUGGAGE.
examples: Thin boys were lugging sacks of wheat flour.
She was lugging two heavy bags up the stairs.

meaning: A soft, gentle song sung to make a baby sleep
trick: LULL + a BYE-bye: a song that lulls baby to sleep.
examples: He bounced her in his arms and hummed a lullaby.
My mother sang me a lullaby every night.

meaning: A solid piece of something with no clear shape; also a small swelling on the body
trick: LUMP = a lumpy, bumpy piece.
examples: My upper body felt like a lump of dough.
She put a lump of sugar in her tea.

usage.pattern: a lump of something / a lump in/on something

meaning: (formal, old-fashioned) a lunch, often a formal one
trick: LUNCHEON = a fancy LUNCH.
examples: I proposed she should have luncheon with me.
The club holds a luncheon for its members every year.

usage.pattern: have luncheon (with someone) / a luncheon for someone

meaning: Moved forward suddenly and forcefully, often to attack
trick: LUNGED: a sudden leap with full LUNGS of air.
examples: He bared his yellow teeth and lunged at me.
The dog lunged at the postman.

usage.pattern: lunged at someone / lunged for something

meaning: Made a sudden, unsteady movement; also moved in an unsteady, swaying way
trick: LURCHED: the bus LURCHED and everyone fell forward.
examples: He lurched across the yard and kicked off his boots.
The bus lurched forward and I grabbed the rail.

meaning: Something that strongly attracts or tempts people; also to tempt someone
trick: LURE = a fishing bait that LURES fish in.
examples: It's tough to ignore that kind of glittering lure.
The lure of city life pulls many young people from villages.

usage.pattern: the lure of something / lure someone into something

meaning: Was present but hidden, often waiting to cause harm
trick: LURKED: like a wolf LURKING in the dark.
examples: She could hear the insincerity that had always lurked beneath.
A thief lurked in the shadows of the alley.

meaning: (of plants) growing thickly and healthily; also rich and comfortable
trick: LUSH: rain makes everything LUSH green.
examples: The valley below was carpeted by lush farming fields.
After the monsoon, the hills were lush and green.

meaning: Rich and plentiful; (of plants or hair) growing thickly and well
trick: LUXURIANT = LUXURY-rich and abundant.
examples: A new life, luxuriant with possibility and joy.
She had luxuriant black hair down to her waist.

usage.pattern: luxuriant + noun / be luxuriant with something

meaning: Expressing feelings in a beautiful, poetic way, like a song
trick: LYRICAL = like song LYRICS.
examples: The novel is written in often lyrical prose.
The writer gave a lyrical description of the sunset.

usage.pattern: lyrical + noun / wax lyrical about something
